findings.text: Independent adversarial review at 7544b14: pass_with_notes, 0 blocking. The highest-risk claim (hook-less enforcement, NG2) was behaviorally cleared: the git pre-push hook feeds scripts/warp-guard.sh the JSON payload on stdin (tool_input.command), NOT the env CMD the guard ignores, so an unproven push EXITS 2 (blocks), a proven push (green last_verify commit==HEAD + proof for HEAD) EXITS 0 (allows), a wrong-commit EXITS 2 (commit-bound), and a missing guard EXITS 1 (fail-closed); env CMD + empty stdin reproduced the W3 fail-open (exit 0), confirming stdin is the only live channel. copilot-instructions.md documents enabling both the git hook (core.hooksPath) and the required CI status check, and warp-gate.yml actually runs verify.sh + policy_check server-side. Enforcement is NOT weaker than a local-hook tool.

Three non-blocking notes: (1) the Copilot instruction/prompt/agent format is plausible current idiom on a fast-moving surface (the spec flags this; the guaranteed enforcement does not depend on it); (2) both enforcement mechanisms need one-time human enablement (git config core.hooksPath hooks; setting the required status check in branch protection) - inherent to the git/hook-less model, documented honestly, true of every pack, not a Copilot-specific weakening; (3) the copilot selftest reuses the shared drift machinery rather than a copilot-specific temp-clone mutation - teeth still real (re-proven directly on the copilot copy), a stylistic asymmetry.
